title: Who killed JFK?
summary: Josh and Chuck, with guest producer Matt, examine the November 22, 1963 assassination of President John F. Kennedy in Dallas and the main conspiracy theories around it. They walk through the motorcade route and events at Dealey Plaza, the shots and the so-called "magic bullet," the Texas School Book Depository and the sniper's nest, the shooting of Officer J.D. Tippett, Oswald's arrest at the Texas Theater, and his background (Marine Corps, defection to the USSR, attempt on General Edwin Walker, New Orleans pro-Castro activity). They cover Jack Ruby's killing of Oswald, the Warren Commission's lone-gunman conclusion, the 1976 House Select Committee on Assassinations' conspiracy finding, the Rockefeller Commission, and theories involving the mafia, the CIA, the KGB or Cuba, and Lyndon Johnson, plus the three tramps theory and George de Mohrenschildt-era CIA links (George Joannides). The episode ends with a listener mail about a listener in Wuhan, China who used the zombie episode for a lesson, and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and framing the JFK assassination
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode, the upcoming 50th anniversary, the ABC News poll on belief in a broader plot, and the cultural staying power of the conspiracy theories. They say they will only skim the topic.

segments.title: Kennedy's Dallas trip and the motorcade
segments.summary: Kennedy's trip to Texas to unite feuding Texas Democrats Connally and Yarborough, the publicized route, and the motorcade from Love Field toward Dealey Plaza.

segments.title: The shooting in Dealey Plaza and the magic bullet
segments.summary: Accounts of the shots at about 12:30 pm, the wounds to Kennedy and Connally, the magic bullet theory, and Jackie Kennedy's reaction and the brain-tissue account.

segments.title: Grassy Knoll, acoustics, and Kennedy's death
segments.summary: Confusing witness accounts and the acoustics of Dealey Plaza fuel the grassy knoll theory, including Officer Clyde Hay running toward the knoll. Kennedy is pronounced dead at Parkland at about 1 pm, and Johnson is sworn in aboard Air Force One.
